newsitem.title: USA: FPL sees Turkey Pt 3 nuclear unit up by Fri.
newsitem.headline: FPL sees Turkey Pt 3 nuclear unit up by Fri.

text.p: Florida Power & Light Co's (FP&L) Turkey Point 3 nuclear unit was expected to resume operation by Friday, the company said Thursday.
"It'll be by the end of the week, either today or tomorrow...more likely tomorrow," said company spokeswoman Janice Brady, when asked about the current restart schedule.
The utility shut the 666 megawatt (MW) generating unit in Florida City, Fla., after two of its 45 control rods dropped accidently into the reactor early Tuesday.
The control rod assembly regulates the nuclear fission process inside the reactor core.
FP&L on Tuesday said it would take two to three days to correct the situation.
The neighboring Turkey Point 4 nuclear unit, also 666 MW, was operating at full output.
The Turkey Point facility also has two 810 MW coal-fired power generation units.

FP&L is the operator and sole owner of the Turkey Point nuclear units. The utility also operates two 839 MW nuclear units at the St Lucie generating complex on Hutchinson Island off the east coast of Florida.
The four nuclear units account for approximately a fourth of the utility's installed generating capacity.
Florida Power & Light, a subsidiary of FP&L Group, Inc, provides electric service to parts or entire parts of 35 counties in the southern and eastern Florida pennisula.
FP&L is headquartered in Juno Beach, Fla.
